description: SECURITY TAG | Static Application Security Testing analyzes source code or compiled representations without executing the application to identify potential vulnerabilities early in development.
SECURITY TAG | Dynamic Application Security Testing examines a running application from the outside to identify vulnerabilities such as injection flaws and configuration weaknesses.
SECURITY TAG | Interactive Application Security Testing analyzes application behavior during execution, often using instrumentation to identify vulnerabilities.
SECURITY TAG | Software Composition Analysis identifies third-party software components, vulnerable dependencies, and potential open-source license compliance issues.
SECURITY TAG | Software Bill of Materials inventories software components and dependencies, helping organizations identify vulnerable libraries and manage supply chain risks.
SECURITY TAG | Common Weakness Enumeration categorizes software and hardware weakness types, helping security professionals identify recurring vulnerability patterns.
SECURITY TAG | Indicator of Compromise is evidence suggesting a system may be compromised, such as malicious file hashes, suspicious IP addresses, or unexpected processes.
SECURITY TAG | Indicator of Attack identifies suspicious behaviors or activities associated with an ongoing or attempted attack rather than relying only on known compromise artifacts.
SECURITY TAG | Breach and Attack Simulation safely simulates adversarial techniques to evaluate security controls and identify defensive gaps.
SECURITY TAG | Penetration Testing is authorized security testing that attempts to exploit vulnerabilities to demonstrate potential impact and validate defenses.
SECURITY TAG | Address Space Layout Randomization randomizes memory locations used by programs, making exploitation more difficult by reducing predictability.
SECURITY TAG | Data Execution Prevention marks certain memory regions as non-executable, helping prevent attackers from executing malicious code in data-only memory areas.
SECURITY TAG | Runtime Application Self-Protection monitors an application during execution and can detect or block attacks from within the running application.
SECURITY TAG | Remote Access Trojan is malware that provides an attacker with unauthorized remote access to a compromised system.
SECURITY TAG | Command and Control refers to infrastructure or communication channels attackers use to remotely control compromised systems and issue malicious instructions.
SECURITY TAG | Command and Control is attacker infrastructure used to communicate with compromised devices, coordinate malicious activity, and distribute commands.
SECURITY TAG | Potentially Unwanted Program is software that may be undesirable because of intrusive behavior, bundled installations, privacy concerns, or unwanted system changes.
SECURITY TAG | Bring Your Own Device allows employees to use personal devices for work, introducing security concerns involving data separation, access control, and device management.
SECURITY TAG | Corporate-Owned, Personally Enabled describes organization-owned devices that employees may also use for approved personal activities.
SECURITY TAG | Choose Your Own Device allows employees to select work devices from an organization-approved list, balancing user preference with security requirements.
SECURITY TAG | Mobile Device Management centrally configures, monitors, and enforces security policies on mobile devices, including screen locks, encryption, and remote wiping.
SECURITY TAG | Mobile Application Management controls and secures applications and their data on mobile devices, potentially without managing the entire device.
SECURITY TAG | Internet of Things describes connected physical devices that collect, exchange, or act on data, often introducing risks from weak credentials and limited patching.
SECURITY TAG | Operational Technology includes hardware and software that monitors or controls physical processes, where safety and availability are often critical.
SECURITY TAG | Industrial Control Systems monitor or control industrial processes and may include programmable logic controllers, supervisory systems, and operator interfaces.
SECURITY TAG | Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems remotely monitor and control industrial processes, collecting field data and supporting centralized supervisory operations.
SECURITY TAG | Programmable Logic Controller is an industrial computer that executes control logic to operate machinery, equipment, and automated physical processes.
SECURITY TAG | Human-Machine Interface allows operators to monitor industrial processes, view system status, and issue commands to control equipment.
